A Bar continues at this address and is to be intensified. A new Bar would be a conditional use here, and a conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without a new Conditional Use (Planning Code § 178; this text in force since before 2022-01-01).
Zoning district NCD-HAIGHT: Nighttime Entertainment on the first story is a conditional use (Planning Code § 719, in force since before 2022-01-01).

Nighttime Entertainment continues at this address and is to be intensified. A new Nighttime Entertainment would be a conditional use here, and a conditional use may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without a new Conditional Use (Planning Code § 178; this text in force since before 2022-01-01).

triggers.label: Liquor licence rule of a restricted district

lines.text: Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict: A new on-sale liquor establishment (ABC Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57: bars and restaurants serving alcohol) needs Conditional Use. The concept needs ABC Type 90, which is not one of the licence types this rule reaches (Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48 and 57), so it was not applied (Planning Code § 781.9(c)(2), in force from 2024-01-14 (Ord. 249-23, File No. 230701)).

Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict: ABC licence Types 51, 52, 59, 60, 61, 64, 67, 70, 75 and 90 are not 'on-sale liquor establishments', so the Conditional Use rule for new on-sale establishments does not reach them. Types 64 and 90 were added to the list. The concept needs ABC Type 90, which this rule names (Planning Code § 781.9(c)(1)(B), in force from 2024-01-14 (Ord. 249-23, File No. 230701)).

neighbourhood_notice_lines.text: Under the Planning Code as in force on 4 June 2025, a change of use does not by itself need neighbourhood notice: the change-of-use trigger has been out of Planning Code § 311 since 14 January 2024 (Ord. 248-23, File No. 230446). Notice for work that enlarges a building, and for demolition or new construction, is a separate question the rules did not check.

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)
